ingredients.item: baby octopus , cleaned — beaks and innards removed, bodies left whole; thawed fully and patted dry if frozen
gochugaru — the heat dial for the drinking table
Steamed rice , mu sangchae or cucumber banchan , soju's ceremony

instructions.heading: Onion down first, octopus over
instructions.action: Onion down first, octopus over. Lay the onion arcs across the hot oiled pan as a bed, and spread the marinated jjukkumi over and around them in a single layer — the bodies will curl and the tentacles tighten into little crowns as they hit.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: a hard sizzle and steam rising off the marinade's water, sweet chile in the air within a minute. If the pan is quiet and pooling liquid, it was not hot enough — pull the batch, reheat, restart; jjukkumi boiled in marinade is rubber in glaze.

instructions.heading: Turn with the tongs, two minutes at a time, glaze as it reduces
instructions.action: Turn with the tongs, two minutes at a time, glaze as it reduces. The marinade's water cooks off and what remains on the pan thickens to a glaze that lacquers each octopus as you turn them through it — four to six minutes total. Scallions in for the last two. The bodies are done when they are firm-plump, glossy red-brown, and a body cut at the pan reads opaque to its center.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the pan should be nearly dry, everything coated brick-glossy, onion edges char-sweet and translucent. One test octopus whole: snap-tender (they are small — this is the tender side of octopus's law), sweet-heat lacquer, the ocean's sweetness under it. If any bite is rubbery, that piece needed one more minute in the reducing glaze — small octopus tenderizes briefly under heat before it tightens, unl

instructions.heading: Pan to the table on its trivet, sesame over, straight off the pan
instructions.action: Pan to the table on its trivet, sesame over, straight off the pan. Jjukkumi's window is while the glaze still sizzles; rice in one hand, tongs in the other, the cabbage or perilla to wrap the sweetest, hottest ones.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the table test: a whole octopus over rice in one bite-set — glaze edge, snap, chew, heat blooming late — with the cold radish between rounds. The platter should be empty before the pan stops sizzling; that is not a metaphor, it is the recipe's honest clock.

visualDonenessCues: The octopus: beaked and cleaned, dried, marinated 30 minutes, whole.
The pan: hot enough to sizzle hard on landing; onion bed down first; glaze reduces to lacquer in 4–6 minutes.
The pull: firm-plump glossy bodies, opaque at a test cut, snap-tender at the tooth.
The table: off the sizzling pan, rice and cold crunch in reach, platter empty before the pan cools.
storageNotes: Marinated jjukkumi hold 24 hours refrigerated. Cooked, 2 days — chopped into fried rice or bibim-guksu (cold spicy noodles), where the leftover glaze seasons the whole bowl.

Variations: the big-octopus fork with the pre-simmer (#SF05); squid takes this same marinade and the #SF04 clock; a handful of rice cakes tossed onto the pan in the last three minutes is the tent's carb course and entirely correct.
